chapter: Looking back and the lean years
title: The audition again, losing the California house, and the end of studio jobs
summary: He repeats the three-of-six audition story, and explains that studio men no longer get staff pay, so he lost his house and returned east.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: But, it was just a magnificent band and that was an occasion where he had that one job-- now after that, well, we had nothing; you couldn't give the band away. You just couldn't give it away. And, I told you that story aboutthe time a guy called me and said - I hear you got a good band - and where are you working - I'd like to hear you and I said - well, we're not working this week but-- I never make auditions which I haven't for years; if you want to hear the band, I'll bring it over to your club in the afternoon, which is okay with the union to do such a thing - to make an audition - so we went over and we played all our best numbers and everything - and I said to the fellows - well, go home - and I'll give you a call - see what the man says -- and the guy was sitting there with his girl and some other guy and he said - 'well, you've got a hell of a band' - he said, 'I can use three of you' -- he can use three out of my band -- now, I was so mad, I just walked out.

Instead of him telling me of course - I can use a three-piece band, he wants to hear all six of them -- but this was what I was up against and in California, it got to be to the point where I couldn't make the payments on my house or anything. If I stayed there, I would have been gone by now. There was nothing there. And, I still think to this day, I wonder how those guys make it out there.

Studio -- well, there isn't that much studio work around anymore. You see, what they do in those days, in the beginning, when those guys all got well, and bought houses which they own now, but they were working in the studio bands; but they were getting paid whether they worked or not. Now, when they make a picture - they say okay - we're all set and I'll call a band in and we'll get this over with in a hurry. So, they call musicians in to do the picture - bang - out of work again. But, in those days, it didn't use to be that way-- you were what you call the staff band.

I never got on the staff although I did do - while I was out there - did a couple of sound tracks which mean nothing. Just with other group of guys playing this and that and something else. But, on that occasion, I lost my house and I had to go back -- and, at that time, again, all my work was back East. I kept getting calls to come back there and I went back.
